fields.v:
Agent = Codex CLI for all; 42 test sessions x 5 seeds = 210 replays; <= 6 turns. Criterion per replay: LLM-judge score 0-100 (SWE-chat rubric); also follow-up rate and win/tie/loss vs A (Tables 1, 2, 5). The authors state no success threshold for a configuration (the rubric's bands, e.g. 60-69 'partial success', p. 18, grade single replays), so quality verdict for every entry: no criterion stated by the authors. Cost measured only for the four Sol-low/Sol-low conditions (Table 6, agent tokens and execution time per replay); cost verdict: no criterion stated by the authors where measured, 'not measured' otherwise.
Generator GPT-5.6 Sol-low:
- (A) No skill + Codex CLI + GPT-5.6 Sol-low: 65.27 +/- 1.94; follow-up 24.76%; 442,096 tokens, 91.76 s
- (B) Personalized + Codex CLI + GPT-5.6 Sol-low: 67.64 +/- 2.71 (p = .084); 30.95%; W/T/L 51.90/7.62/40.48%; 597,120 tokens, 106.16 s
- (C) Random developer skill + Codex CLI + Sol-low: 67.75 +/- 3.68; 27.62%; W/T/L 50.95/10.48/38.57%; 521,219 tokens, 99.62 s
- (D) Generic skill + Codex CLI + Sol-low: 68.38 +/- 1.72 (p = .003); 30.00%; W/T/L 55.71/7.62/36.67%; 643,578 tokens, 104.57 s
- (E, ablation) Rule-based bootstrap only + Sol-low: 67.49 +/- 3.00; cost not measured
- (F, ablation) Leave-one-out generic + Sol-low: 68.37 +/- 1.88; cost not measured
- (A) + Codex CLI + GPT-5.6 Sol-high: 68.59 +/- 4.39; 27.62%; cost not measured
- (B) + Codex CLI + GPT-5.6 Sol-high: 66.71 +/- 7.34; 25.71%; W/T/L 47.62/7.62/44.76%; cost not measured
- (A) + Codex CLI + GPT-5.6 Sol-max: 70.22 +/- 1.33; 26.19%; cost not measured
- (B) + Codex CLI + GPT-5.6 Sol-max: 72.04 +/- 2.18 (p = .031); 29.05%; W/T/L 53.33/11.43/35.24%; cost not measured
- (A) + Codex CLI + GPT-6 Astra-medium: 65.40 +/- 3.35; 32.38%; cost not measured
- (B) + Codex CLI + GPT-6 Astra-medium: 65.59 +/- 4.34; 37.14%; W/T/L 47.62/12.86/39.52%; cost not measured
Generator GPT-6 Astra-medium (A rows are separate runs; cost not measured):
- (A) / (B) + Sol-low: 63.26 +/- 1.15 / 63.07 +/- 0.62; follow-up 13.81% / 12.38%; B W/T/L 48.10/9.52/42.38%
- (A) / (B) + Sol-high: 63.14 +/- 4.08 / 66.41 +/- 5.90; 10.95% / 11.43%; B W/T/L 55.24/10.95/33.81%
- (A) / (B) + Sol-max: 71.43 +/- 2.82 / 72.33 +/- 3.62; 30.48% / 25.71%; B W/T/L 47.14/7.14/45.71%
- (A) / (B) + Astra-medium: 64.95 +/- 2.94 / 65.91 +/- 3.47; 35.71% / 28.10%; B W/T/L 52.38/11.90/35.71%

Configurations: 2 skill generators x 4 executors x {A, B}; plus A-D on Sol-low/Sol-low and ablations E, F. Baseline: no skill. Held constant: repository commit (isolated worktree), first-turn request, task summary, simulator, scorer, prompts, replay settings, turn limit 6. Acceptance tests: none executable; LLM judge with 100-point SWE-chat rubric. Repetitions: 5 seeds of the data split. Human intervention: none (LLM simulator)

fields.v: Personalized skill beats no skill in 6 of 8 generator-executor pairs, but only one significant (Sol-max with Sol-low skills, +1.82, p = .031); differences range -1.88 to +3.27. On Sol-low/Sol-low: generic skill best (68.38, +3.11, p = .003); personalized +2.37 (n.s., p = .084); random-developer skill 67.75 similar to personalized (B vs C p = .838; D vs B p = .392). Skills raise follow-up rate (24.76% -> 30.95% personalized, 30.00% generic), tokens (+35% personalized, +46% generic) and time. Personalized skill helps when >= 6 relevant evolution sessions (B-A +10.17, B-C +8.92, B-D +5.67), not otherwise. Refinement adds little over bootstrap (67.64 vs 67.49, p = .886)

fields.v: Distinguished generic skill from no skill; did not reliably distinguish personalized vs other conditions (most differences n.s., large SD). Repeatability: 5 seeds with paired t-tests over seed means. Simulator validated: 89.47% of follow-ups at least partially match real developer messages. Limitations stated: small filtered sample, simulator may not reproduce humans, LLM-based scoring biases, no executable tests, reconstructed repos may lack dependencies

fields.v: Small, highly filtered SWE-chat subset (206 sessions, 13 developers) may bias towards particular developers, repos and task types; limited per-developer history; LLM simulator approximates collaboration, follow-up rate is not real efficiency; task summarization, skill generation and LLM scoring may add model-dependent biases; LLM evaluation cannot replace tests or humans; random (not chronological) split assumes static preferences; only prompt-injected natural-language skills. Future: longer traces, other skill-integration methods, retrieval of task-relevant guidance combined with developer preferences
